title: 第22章 门第22章 镜中人
slug: 黯潮纪元异世界的崛起
content_zh:
陈默掌心的圣光在暗金色与黑色之间流动，像某种活物的心跳。
值班室里的空气凝固了。塞西尔后退半步，后背撞上窗沿。黎明前的冷风从窗外灌进来，吹动他额前的白发。他盯着陈默的手掌，瞳孔微微收缩——不是恐惧，是审视。
“结束了。”塞西尔说。
“什么？”
“你的话。”塞西尔的声音恢复了平静，“你说得太直白了。不像一个会藏秘密的人。”
陈默愣了一下。
塞西尔从怀里掏出那封信，当着陈默的面撕成两半，扔进旁边的火盆。纸页卷曲、燃烧、变成灰烬。
“那封信是假的。”塞西尔说，“我写的。”
“你——”
“我需要确认一件事。”塞西尔打断他，“确认你是否知道自己是什么。”
陈默掌心的圣光熄灭了。他盯着火盆里燃烧的纸灰，感觉脑子里有什么东西在重新排列——像拼图碎片突然找到正确的位置。
“你一直在试探我。”陈默说。
“从你进入银月城的第一天。”塞西尔点头，“阿尔德里奇失踪，法师塔封锁，调令——都是我安排的。”
“为什么？”
“因为黯潮的斥候在你身边出现过三次。”塞西尔的声音变低了，“第一次在你进入城墙的当晚，第二次在图书馆地下，第三次——”他顿了顿，“在艾莉西亚的训练场。”
陈默的手指收紧。他想起那天下午，艾莉西亚在训练场上摔倒，德文·铁卫的剑差点刺穿她的肩膀。那只是意外吗？
“斥候不会主动攻击。”塞西尔说，“它们在观察。观察你，观察你身边的人，观察你的反应。”
“它们在找什么？”
“找你的弱点。”塞西尔转过身，面对窗外。东边的天空已经开始泛白，第一缕阳光刺破云层，在城墙上拉出一道金色的线，“也找你的极限。”
陈默沉默了。

塞西尔没有回头，继续说：“阿尔德里奇失踪之前，留了一份文件。他称你为‘门’——不是拯救者，不是毁灭者，只是一扇门。”
“门后面是什么？”
“不知道。”塞西尔说，“阿尔德里奇也没找到答案。他只找到了一句话，刻在法师塔地下三层的墙壁上，用一种失传的古代文字。”
他停顿了一下。
“门若打开，万物归墟。”
陈默感觉后颈的汗毛又竖了起来。那句话像一根针，扎进他的意识深处。
“所以你制造了这场戏。”陈默说，“引我到哨塔，让斥候出现，测试我的圣光反应。”
“我需要知道你的圣光是否可控。”塞西尔说，“现在我知道了。”
“可控吗？”
“不可控。”塞西尔转身，直视他的眼睛，“但也不是完全失控。你的圣光有自己的意志——它在保护你，也在保护自己。”
陈默低头看自己的手掌。圣光已经彻底消退，皮肤上什么痕迹都没留下。但他能感觉到，那股力量还在，像沉睡的野兽蜷缩在意识深处，随时可能醒来。
“接下来怎么办？”他问。
“你继续执行任务。”塞西尔说，“但不要再靠近法师塔。”
“为什么？”
“因为塔里的东西——不是黯潮。”塞西尔的声音变得很轻，像怕被什么东西听到，“是另一种东西。比黯潮更古老，更危险。”
陈默正要追问，窗外传来急促的脚步声。
塞西尔皱眉，走到窗边往外看。陈默跟过去——街道上，一个穿着圣殿骑士团制服的士兵正在奔跑，方向是东城门。
“出事了。”塞西尔说。
他们下楼时，值班室的门被撞开。那个士兵冲进来，脸色惨白，呼吸急促得像拉风箱。
“特使大人——”他喘着气，“城外废墟——发现了尸体。”

“谁的？”
“阿尔德里奇大法师的。”
陈默感觉脑子里有什么东西炸开了。
***
content_en:
The holy light in Chen Mo's palm flows between dark gold and black, like the heartbeat of some living creature.
The air in the duty room solidified. Cecil took half a step back, and his back hit the window edge. The cold wind before dawn poured in from the window, blowing the white hair on his forehead. He stared at Chen Mo's palm, his pupils shrinking slightly - not out of fear, but out of scrutiny.
"It's over," Cecil said.
"What?"
"Your words." Cecil's voice regained its calmness, "You speak too frankly. You don't look like a person who hides secrets."
Chen Mo was stunned for a moment.
Cecil took out the letter from his arms, tore it in half in front of Chen Mo, and threw it into the brazier next to him. The pages curled, burned, turned to ash.
"That letter is a fake," Cecil said. "I wrote it."
"You——"
"I need to confirm something." Cecil interrupted, "make sure you know what you are."
The holy light in Chen Mo's palm went out. He stared at the burning paper ashes in the brazier and felt something rearranging in his mind - like pieces of a puzzle suddenly finding their correct place.
"You have been testing me." Chen Mo said.
"From the first day you entered Silvermoon City." Cecil nodded, "Aldridge disappeared, the mage tower was blocked, and the orders were transferred—all were arranged by me."
"Why?"
"Because the scouts of the Dark Tide appeared around you three times." Cecil's voice became lower. "The first time was on the night you entered the city wall, the second time was underground in the library, and the third time -" he paused, "at Alicia's training ground."
Chen Mo tightened his fingers. He thought of that afternoon, when Alicia fell on the training ground and Devin Ironguard's sword nearly pierced her shoulder. Was that just an accident?
"Scouts don't actively attack," Cecil said. "They are observing. Observing you, observing the people around you, and observing your reactions."
"What are they looking for?"
"Look for your weakness." Cecil turned around and faced the window. The sky in the east has begun to turn white, and the first ray of sunlight pierces the clouds, drawing a golden line on the city wall, "Find your limit too."
Chen Mo was silent.
Cecil did not look back and continued: "Before Aldridge disappeared, he left a document. He called you 'the door' - not a savior, not a destroyer, just a door."
"What's behind the door?"
"I don't know," Cecil said. "Aldridge didn't find the answer either. He only found a sentence, carved on the wall of the third underground floor of the Mage Tower, in a lost ancient script."
He paused.
"If the door is opened, everything will return to ruins."
Chen Mo felt the hairs on the back of his neck stand up again. Those words were like a needle piercing into the depths of his consciousness.
"So you created this scene." Chen Mo said, "Lead me to the sentry tower and let the scouts appear to test my reaction to the Holy Light."
"I needed to know if your Light was controllable," Cecil said. "Now I know."
"Is it controllable?"
"It's out of control." Cecil turned around and looked directly into his eyes, "But it's not completely out of control. Your Holy Light has its own will - it's protecting you and itself."
Chen Mo looked down at his palms. The holy light has completely faded away, leaving no trace on the skin. But he could feel that the power was still there, curled up in the depths of his consciousness like a sleeping beast that might wake up at any time.
"What's next?" he asked.
"You continue your mission," Cecil said, "but don't come near the Mage Tower again."
"Why?"
"Because the thing in the tower is not the Dark Tide." Cecil's voice became very soft, as if he was afraid of being heard by something. "It is another thing. It is older and more dangerous than the Dark Tide."
Chen Mo was about to ask further questions when rapid footsteps came from outside the window.
Cecil frowned, walked to the window and looked out. Chen Mo followed him - on the street, a man dressed as a TemplarSoldiers in regimental uniforms are running towards the east gate.
"Something's wrong," Cecil said.
When they went downstairs, the door to the duty room was knocked open. The soldier rushed in, his face was pale, and his breathing was as rapid as a bellows.
"My lord envoy -" he gasped, "the corpse was found in the ruins outside the city."
"Whose?"
"It belongs to Archmage Aldridge."
Chen Mo felt like something exploded in his head.
***
